status: authored G0 generation; no independent validation, runtime, simulation or playtest
frame: One selected hero; three stages with a boss in each; mid-stage acquisitions; manual execution or player-authored auto. These candidate operations can occupy encounters or optional item slices within that frame.

evidence_delivery.timing: During G0 after input reading and before saving the pool
evidence_delivery.content: Parent reported ECHO developer precedent for visible short-lived enemy learning, cooperation and betrayal; Mosa Lina official description opposes lock/key tools through randomized handmade tools/levels.
evidence_delivery.effect: Enemy learning or cooperation alone is treated as familiar; extra relationships remain hypotheses for subsequent comparison. This pass was not blinded.

claim_ceiling: Written construction and distinction from supplied portfolio only. Possible equivalents are comparison hypotheses, not verified prior-art findings or absence claims.

variants.title: The enemy courier delivers your amended attack order
variants.concrete_rule: One courier carries a sweep-lane card to a boss lectern. Before delivery, spend a seal to replace east with west or reverse; delivery locks the next eligible sweep there. Destroying the courier cancels the amendment without refund.
variants.player_choice: Intercept and preserve the courier, or fight it and retain the ordinary sweep.
variants.cost: One finite seal, exposed interception and surviving the delivery interval.
variants.feedback: Card face, courier route, arrival deadline and locked lane are public.
variants.manual_auto: Both issue intercept/amend commands; auto requires authored courier-preservation and escape rules.
variants.illustrative_encounter: Redirect the sweep through adds, then stop attacking its dangerous messenger.
variants.distinct_from_prior_portfolio: The enemy transports a changeable instruction before commitment, rather than drawing a spell or reporting a build counter.
variants.possible_equivalent: Delayed attack redirection plus escort; enemy cooperation alone is familiar.
variants.open_question: Does physically preserving the courier add a viable choice beyond delayed targeting?

variants.title: Your pursuer certifies the emergency exit
variants.concrete_rule: An inspector records two turns while pursuing. Finishing at a booth prints one certificate. Installing it opens a gate for the next actor that repeats those turns; the certificate is then consumed.
variants.player_choice: Teach an easy route for reliable access, or a demanding route enemies are less likely to execute.
variants.cost: Exposure during certification and one finite gate slot.
variants.feedback: Two recorded arrows, certificate carrier and gate's remaining use are shown.
variants.manual_auto: Manual executes the route; auto authors certification, collection and later matching routes.
variants.illustrative_encounter: A short certificate eases escape but lets the chasing add consume the exit first.
variants.distinct_from_prior_portfolio: The learned route becomes transferable one-use permission, rather than a spell or enemy prediction.
variants.open_question: Can route identity be readable without onerous exact-position matching?

variants.title: Monsters carry your performance review
variants.concrete_rule: A witness records the first guard, dodge and skill it sees, up to three records. Defeating it yields the recorded XP once; escaping witnesses remove that XP opportunity from the stage budget.
variants.player_choice: Demonstrate more actions for later XP or kill the witness before it escapes.
variants.cost: Time, exposure and deferred reward; no repeated records or new encounter budget.
variants.feedback: Visible record icons and a marked escape route.
variants.manual_auto: Both can perform the three actions; auto must author the demonstrations explicitly.
variants.illustrative_encounter: A witness near a poison pool offers one last record at dangerous cost.
variants.distinct_from_prior_portfolio: A moving enemy carries action-specific deferred progression.
variants.possible_equivalent: Challenge-based bonus XP attached to a fleeing loot enemy.
variants.open_question: Is this anything beyond those familiar mechanisms joined together?

variants.title: Interrupted spells build a room nobody can finish casting inside
variants.concrete_rule: Three distinct interruption marks define one eight-second triangle. An eligible spell started inside completes only if its caster crosses outside before recovery ends; otherwise it fizzles. Ordinary movement and melee remain legal.
variants.player_choice: Lure a stationary caster inside, or start your own cast there and exit during commitment.
variants.cost: Three lost casts, one region capacity and dangerous exit timing.
variants.feedback: Visible vertices, boundary and per-cast exit requirement.
variants.manual_auto: Both need cast-origin and crossing observations; auto authors the exit segment.
variants.illustrative_encounter: Interruptions near a mage form shelter that the hero must leave to retaliate magically.
variants.distinct_from_prior_portfolio: Failure creates shared action jurisdiction, rather than ink walls or damage anchors.
variants.open_question: Can this preserve enough feasible casting windows to avoid blanket denial?

variants.title: A broken guard gives you right of way against the traffic
variants.concrete_rule: After a guard break, claim the retained segment once. For six seconds, hero acceleration along it activates only while one grounded enemy traverses in the opposite direction; enemies receive ordinary movement.
variants.player_choice: Invite hostile traffic to accelerate an escape, or avoid contact and abandon the residue.
variants.cost: The original damage and guard loss remain; claiming spends recovery.
variants.feedback: Corridor arrows and current eligibility glow.
variants.manual_auto: Auto needs public traversal direction and an explicit opposing route; no invisible route creation.
variants.illustrative_encounter: A charging add finances the retreat toward a cache but creates collision risk.
variants.distinct_from_prior_portfolio: A failed defense makes motion depend on opposing traffic, not contact-powered retaliation.
variants.possible_equivalent: Conditional movement boosts and one-way traffic puzzles.
variants.open_question: Can useful opposite travel occur without requiring unavoidable damage?

variants.title: Your failed attacks make a moat for the healthy
variants.concrete_rule: Up to three missed spells leave adjacent pits. Their union slows actors above half health for eight seconds; actors below the threshold move normally. No damage or additional spell resource is created.
variants.player_choice: Place misses to slow healthy pursuers, or preserve charges and use ordinary movement.
variants.cost: Lost spell charges, cast recovery and the possibility of slowing yourself.
variants.feedback: Pit edges, lifetime and threshold status are visible.
variants.manual_auto: Both target misses; auto requires health-reserve and placement predicates.
variants.illustrative_encounter: An injured hero crosses a strip but newly healing above the threshold changes the exit cost.
variants.distinct_from_prior_portfolio: Health changes traversal permission within failed-cast geometry.
variants.possible_equivalent: A health-conditioned slow field with missed-spell placement.
variants.open_question: Does the threshold add a worthwhile decision beyond ordinary status terrain?

variants.title: Teach the boss your escape handwriting
variants.concrete_rule: Spend a charge to draw two legal segments. The next eligible hostile knockback follows them within its existing displacement budget. A marked enemy covers the last repeated endpoint; both memories and the new gesture are public.
variants.player_choice: Repeat a useful escape to prepare the enemy, then revise it; or avoid teaching and accept normal displacement.
variants.cost: Drawing recovery, charge and commitment to the drawn turn sequence.
variants.feedback: Path preview, endpoint memory and pending knockback budget.
variants.manual_auto: Manual draws or selects segments; auto authors the same bounded gesture and reserve.
variants.illustrative_encounter: Two safe rightward shoves teach a guard, then a leftward revision reaches a cache.
variants.distinct_from_prior_portfolio: Learning is coupled to player-authored hostile displacement, not copied musical attacks or route coverage alone.
variants.possible_equivalent: Steered knockback plus visible enemy learning; the latter is familiar.
variants.open_question: Does the drawing determine decisions beyond a directional dodge?

variants.title: The boss learns your punctuation and your items must obey it
variants.concrete_rule: Two completed phrases commit one upcoming boss cycle to the displayed rest slot. During that cycle the hero's selected item can activate only in that slot. One pattern is pending; it cannot overwrite an ongoing cycle.
variants.player_choice: Teach an early rest for immediate utility, or a late rest for an approach before activation.
variants.cost: Two phrase charges, performance recovery and constrained item timing.
variants.feedback: Four-slot score, learned-rest counter and activation eligibility.
variants.manual_auto: Voice/tapping and authored phrase selection share the rule; input uncertainty rejects admission.
variants.illustrative_encounter: A late rest permits walking into poison range before the cleanse can activate.
variants.distinct_from_prior_portfolio: A learned omission jointly restricts both actors' action grammar; MC01 changes enemy intervals and burst power.
variants.possible_equivalent: Rhythm-locked item activation plus an authored boss pause.
variants.open_question: Does the shared restriction remain expressive rather than arbitrary?

variants.title: A perfect note teaches the boss perfect aim
variants.concrete_rule: Complete a phrase at one of three displayed conformity bands. The hero's next burst and one upcoming boss volley receive the band's shared bounded spread. One stored band expires after a single eligible volley.
variants.player_choice: Perform accurately for a focused burst, or choose an alternate band for a wider incoming volley.
variants.cost: Phrase charge, cast commitment and increased incoming precision.
variants.feedback: Both spread cones and stored band are shown.
variants.manual_auto: Calibrated voice or timing controls select the band; full-auto authors it without fake errors.
variants.illustrative_encounter: A focused burst kills an add but the following narrow volley pressures exact dodging.
variants.distinct_from_prior_portfolio: Shared aim rather than shared damage/detection or tempo.
variants.possible_equivalent: A coupled accuracy buff with familiar rhythm input.
variants.open_question: Is its strategic structure different from MC01's coupled tempo benefit and threat?

variants.title: Keep the shove in escrow until you break your silence
variants.concrete_rule: A finite anchor charge defers one eligible knockback for up to four seconds; hit damage resolves normally. The hero's next attack or timeout releases its recorded vector through current collision rules. Guarding and moving do not release it.
variants.player_choice: Move to a safer release location while withholding attack, or attack now and accept the shove.
variants.cost: Charge, original damage, attack delay and displacement debt.
variants.feedback: Stored direction, magnitude, remaining hold and predicted current collision are public.
variants.manual_auto: Auto authors withholding, relocation and release, with no automatic safety correction.
variants.illustrative_encounter: Hold a northward shove, walk behind cover, then attack to release it into the wall.
variants.distinct_from_prior_portfolio: WM16 borrows defense; this preserves and relocates an actual hostile movement obligation.
variants.possible_equivalent: Delayed knockback, rooted charge skills and stored momentum.
variants.open_question: Can hazard scheduling remain fair while an obligatory displacement is pending?

variants.title: Let a recipe forget the first attack
variants.concrete_rule: An exposed retort records two nearby attack categories in order. A visible recipe table maps the pair to a poison jet or gate pulse. Waiting three seconds erases the oldest record, allowing a different next attack to complete the pair. Release spends the retort charge.
variants.player_choice: Cash a valid recipe now or discard its first ingredient by waiting under pressure.
variants.cost: Finite charge, vulnerable retort and lost opportunities during maturation.
variants.feedback: Ordered records, erase timer and eligible outputs.
variants.manual_auto: Both choose location, release and restraint; auto observes public records only.
variants.illustrative_encounter: Ignore a melee-poison pair to seek a ranged-poison recipe that opens the escape gate.
variants.distinct_from_prior_portfolio: A sequence can be pruned through restraint before its rule output is committed.
variants.possible_equivalent: Sequential crafting recipes and charged enemy-response abilities.
variants.open_question: Is enemy-category harvesting distinct from ordinary combo collection?

variants.title: Leave the socket empty to charge the next spell
variants.concrete_rule: An acquired socket stores up to three charge marks from the chosen guard or movement event. Casting discharges all marks as a capped magic bonus; waiting preserves them until their eight-second lifetime expires.
variants.player_choice: Discharge early for safety or accumulate the maximum under pressure.
variants.cost: One item slot, finite encounter-generated marks and foregone earlier casts.
variants.feedback: Charge marks, selected event and earliest expiration.
variants.manual_auto: Both generate legal events and decide when to cast; auto needs an explicit release rule.
variants.illustrative_encounter: Two guards prepare a burst but a ranged phase threatens the final charging opportunity.
variants.distinct_from_prior_portfolio: Selectable source events feed a stored discharge, rather than immediate MC04 effects.
variants.possible_equivalent: Event-charged attacks, combo meters and ordinary capacitor-themed skills.
variants.open_question: Is any decision absent from standard charge mechanics?

variants.title: Defeat the boss by making its attacks unaffordable
variants.concrete_rule: The hero leases one of two marked lanes using finite collateral. A boss charge begun in that lane gains reach but spends two lease tokens instead of one. At zero tokens, its next ordinary recovery opens the arena's defeat seal; direct damage is not required.
variants.player_choice: Lease the dangerous useful lane to exhaust the boss quickly, or endure ordinary charges longer.
variants.cost: Collateral, longer enemy reach and surviving a finite number of commitments.
variants.feedback: Lease map, attack fee and remaining boss tokens.
variants.manual_auto: Both choose lanes and lure attack starts; auto authors approach and escape.
variants.illustrative_encounter: An enhanced charge reaches the cache approach but burns the last two tokens.
variants.distinct_from_prior_portfolio: Enemy empowerment consumes its action entitlement instead of creating reflected damage or slow armor.
variants.possible_equivalent: Boss exhaustion, survival objectives and spatial resource taxation.
variants.open_question: Does the budget create strategy beyond surviving a fixed attack count?

variants.title: Help the boss shine so you can drag its shadow
variants.concrete_rule: A lamp increases boss protection and projects a longer shadow. Spend a hook to tug its endpoint; the boss shifts a bounded distance toward that direction unless geometry blocks it. Dragging it onto three disclosed cuffs ends the phase and permits defeat.
variants.player_choice: Brighten for reachable handles but greater resistance, or use short dangerous close-range handles.
variants.cost: Lamp charge, hook recovery and proximity to the attacking boss.
variants.feedback: Shadow direction, pull limit and cuff progress.
variants.manual_auto: Auto needs lamp, shadow-end and target-direction observations; manual aims the same hooks.
variants.illustrative_encounter: A long shadow reaches cover but its lamp makes the uncuffed boss harder to pressure.
variants.distinct_from_prior_portfolio: Assisting the boss creates a larger indirect manipulation surface, not extra HP followed by slowed armor.
variants.possible_equivalent: Shadow puzzles, indirect boss positioning and protective spotlight mechanics.
variants.open_question: Can shadow projection and displacement be predictable without a complex physical solver?

variants.title: Give the boss a better demolition contract
variants.concrete_rule: A finite taunt charge increases the next eligible boss rush's force. Only that rush can break a marked barrier protecting a defeat seal; the hero must lure the lane and survive. Ordinary combat resumes after opening.
variants.player_choice: Empower one dangerous rush or endure repeated ordinary impacts at the barrier.
variants.cost: Taunt charge, shorter response interval and close positioning.
variants.feedback: Rush force band, target lane and remaining barrier integrity.
variants.manual_auto: Both time the taunt and leave the lane; auto needs a recovery fallback.
variants.illustrative_encounter: An empowered rush opens the seal while exposing the hero to flying debris.
variants.distinct_from_prior_portfolio: Its objective is opening a seal, but the underlying charge redirection strongly overlaps WM02.
variants.possible_equivalent: Boss attacks breaking obstacles and existing empowered-charge proposals.
variants.open_question: Does changing the obstacle's purpose add any new mechanical decision?

variants.title: Let the enemy read the law before you amend one clause
variants.concrete_rule: A placard links crossing a marked east tile to opening gate west. A scout reads and visibly commits its route for one cycle. Spend one amendment to change the source tile to north; the sign shows the change, but the committed route persists until its next inspection.
variants.player_choice: Preserve the useful known rule or amend it after provoking a commitment.
variants.cost: Finite amendment, exposed placard access and the same rule applying to both sides.
variants.feedback: Current clause, scout's last-read clause and locked route.
variants.manual_auto: Both access and amend the sign; auto needs current/read-version predicates.
variants.illustrative_encounter: A flyer bypasses walls but follows its publicly stale gate plan.
variants.distinct_from_prior_portfolio: Public rule versions and delayed enemy inspection replace physical maze obstruction.
variants.possible_equivalent: Rule-editing puzzles, stale-information AI and mutable switches.
variants.open_question: Does versioned inspection add agency beyond an ordinary delayed gate switch?

variants.title: Steal the exception that let the monster cross your wall
variants.concrete_rule: A scout carries one passport granting its bearer one crossing of a marked ward when the bearer matches airborne. At a public booth, spend a seal to replace airborne with grounded. The passport still permits only one crossing and can be dropped or stolen.
variants.player_choice: Alter it for the hero, or leave it unchanged and lure an airborne enemy into spending it.
variants.cost: Seal, exposed collection and one finite use.
variants.feedback: Bearer, current predicate and remaining passage.
variants.manual_auto: Both collect, edit and cross; auto needs bearer and compatibility predicates.
variants.illustrative_encounter: A flyer bypasses the maze; its stolen exception later lets the grounded hero cross a ward.
variants.distinct_from_prior_portfolio: The counter's permission becomes transferable and type-mutable, rather than rebuilding taller walls.
variants.possible_equivalent: Stealing enemy abilities, transferable keys and rule-editable permissions.
variants.open_question: Can the predicate mutation do more than recolor an ordinary key?

variants.title: A trap advertises which enemy class it punishes
variants.concrete_rule: A placed slow trap affects grounded enemies. Spend its single switch charge to replace the target predicate with airborne; the same area, duration and slow remain. Enemies show whether they qualify before entering.
variants.player_choice: Keep the trap useful against walkers or reserve the switch for the announced flyer.
variants.cost: One switch, trap capacity and lost walker coverage after mutation.
variants.feedback: Public class icon, target eligibility and lifetime.
variants.manual_auto: Both switch the flag; auto needs enemy-class and reserve conditions.
variants.illustrative_encounter: Changing coverage helps a flyer phase while leaving grounded adds unslowed.
variants.distinct_from_prior_portfolio: The targeting class is mutable and advertised, although the effect remains ordinary slow.
variants.possible_equivalent: Selectable targeting modes and anti-air upgrades.
variants.open_question: Is the public flag doing anything besides exposing standard targeting state?
